notes: v4.21: Lab Rs/g restored - correction to 4.18: the Labour column IS labour on every format (per-kg on Bill 49, per-gram on 27/06 and stacked bills); Amount is the labour total in all cases, and Lab Rs/g now shows the bill's own rate exactly (132.50, 102.50, 315). 4.18 had wrongly zeroed per-gram labour as a supposed metal rate. v4.20: Less Wt column - the table now shows Less weight between G.Wt and Tunch, in the app and in Excel/PDF exports. Less comes from the bill's own Less/L.Wt. column when printed, else Gross minus Net (identical on every bill checked). v4.19: clean tables - footer lines (Total, Balance, Closing, Bhav rates) no longer appear as items, and nothing after them does either, so a second sheet visible at the photo's bottom edge can't leak rows into the table; quantities now fall back to the Pcs column when a row has no packet lines; Amounts are only picked near the Amount header, so a neighbouring sheet's numbers can't become an item's Amount. The 27/06 bill now reads exactly 7 clean rows. v4.18: automatic tables - just add a bill photo and the table builds itself from the bill. The reader now learns every column from the bill's own header row (L.Wt. is Less, Tunch is purity, Wstg is wastage, Gold column means plain gold, Diamond/Stone columns mean gold-diamond), tells a per-gram metal rate apart from a per-kg labour charge by checking the Amount (so the 27/06 and stacked bills no longer double-count metal as labour), reads plain-gold bills (Bill 22: Gold = Net x (Tunch+Wstg)/100), and ignores numbers from a neighbouring sheet visible at the photo's edge when picking Amounts. Known limits: on gold-diamond (JDM) bills the row finder can still drop rows on some photos (4017 shows 3 real rows); on the stacked silver bill purity is not printed, so type the tunch once per row. v4.17: the reader now uses intelligence instead of fixed positions. It reads each bill's own header row to work out what every column means (L.Wt. is Less, Tunch is purity, Wstg is wastage, a Gold column means plain gold, Diamond/Stone columns mean gold-diamond, a Fine column means silver), and decides silver vs gold from those headers instead of loose keywords - so a silver bill photographed on top of a gold bill no longer flips to gold, and plain gold bills detect correctly. Reading is also ~8x faster: the app now parses from the same OCR pass used for detection instead of re-reading the photo once per preprocessing variant (the old path took ~35 seconds per photo; the parse itself is instant). Known limit: on the stacked silver format the table columns still come from fixed positions, so its rows can misalign - the header column remap for the table itself is the next change. v4.16: fixed silver bills being auto-detected as Gold-Diamond. The old detector counted loose words and fired on the user's own "AURUM DIAMONDS" shop name (dia/diamond) plus 14K fragments from a neighbouring sheet in the photo. Detection now vetoes gold when the bill carries silver evidence (Silver column / silver rate line), requires strong gold evidence (diamond/stone weight-or-rate columns, JDM-style item codes, or the JDM customer name), and no longer counts dia/diamond as gold hints. A standalone Gold column also counts as gold evidence, so plain gold bills (no diamonds, e.g. Bill 22) detect as gold. Also fixed fresh-laptop Setup: it now refuses Python 3.14+ (which cannot resolve the reading-engine packages) and installs/uses Python 3.12 instead, with a one-package-at-a-time pip retry if the combined install fails. v4.15: Automatic format detection for Gold-Diamond estimates (JDM format) and Silver Parchis; fixed Gold table parsing with complete 46-row extraction, lowered Row 1 cutoff threshold, 0.2 degree projection tilt search, and closest-anchor alignment to eliminate row drift. v4.14: separate multipliers in top bar for Making x/g (default 4) and Making x/pc (default 4); Making Charge now displays in its natural unit (/gm or /pc) and calculates customer sell price accordingly; editable Rs/piece column to easily convert any row between piece-rate (/pc) and gram-rate (/gm); scrollable header with mouse-wheel navigation and direct 1:1 click-and-drag scrolling. v4.13: new Rs/piece column (supplier's per-piece rate, e.g. CASTING KADA 55, COIN ARTS 1800); Total Rs/g renamed Supplier Charge and now shows the charge in its natural unit — 55/pp for piece-rate items, 0.30/gm for per-gram items; Making Charge is now rate x mult in the same unit (55x4 = 220 per piece for CASTING KADA). No math changes: MRP / Sell Price identical. v4.12: the reader no longer lets a labour rate land in T+W — when the position-based row search fails (tilted/cropped photo), it now retries on values alone keeping left-to-right order, and the position-based fallback rejects T+W outside 20–200 and skips labour tokens, so a swapped row comes out flagged/incomplete instead of confidently wrong. v4.11: Save Sale now auto-deducts the sold grams from the row's net wt (silver wt, totals and MRP all follow at once); selling more than the net wt left is refused on Save (Calculate only warns); a rapid re-save of the same grams is refused so a double-click can't deduct twice. Deleting a saved sale does not add grams back. v4.10: the frozen header moves with the body on horizontal scrolling even when the mouse is over the header strip. v4.9: Making Charge/g is Making x Total Rs/g (wastage Rs/g + labour Rs/g); the Tunch cell shows the computed purity (a typed tunch still wins and still follows a wastage override). Sell Price is the true MRP: metal = net weight x purity (tunch) / 100 x pure rate, plus customer making per gram x net weight, plus 3% GST. Cost side unchanged (silver weight by T+W, Total Amt). Update-channel build uses the compact recognizer (small detector + tiny reader): same accuracy on clean photos; very poor photos may read slightly worse than the full build. Everything from v4.7 included: fixed column shift, frozen header, PP-OCRv6 engine, rescue pass, loading bar, sell calculator, Save Sale per login with duplicates refused.
